<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, touching **54** documentable anchor(s).

**20** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 162fe54fbbd14d3415a4d72e13abd9a610eedcaf`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **25** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 162fe54fbbd14d3415a4d72e13abd9a610eedcaf` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2930d942e6bcf093f1a98d13054b7e68272bec3d` — the merge of head `a3f4aea3f12ad952ac2ea8b6011f53c3eefb7087` into base `162fe54fbbd14d3415a4d72e13abd9a610eedcaf`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2930d942e6bcf093f1a98d13054b7e68272bec3d && git checkout 2930d942e6bcf093f1a98d13054b7e68272bec3d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 162fe54fbbd14d3415a4d72e13abd9a610eedcaf a3f4aea3f12ad952ac2ea8b6011f53c3eefb7087 && git checkout -B drift-repro 162fe54fbbd14d3415a4d72e13abd9a610eedcaf && git merge --no-ff a3f4aea3f12ad952ac2ea8b6011f53c3eefb7087

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 162fe54fbbd14d3415a4d72e13abd9a610eedcaf
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 162fe54fbbd14d3415a4d72e13abd9a610eedcaf` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

Read: card #34226 with comments 6909048890, 6912081873, 6913134345; the PR body, comments and the net diff against merge-base `5a755791a9` (10 files). No earlier `## Contract review` record exists on this PR.

- **Save door accept-set (`refusePackagedBaseOverride`, `protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts`) — widening, declared right.** The new early return fires only for a `permission` write that names a package, after the read-only named-base limb. `isOwnPermissionSetWrite` answers `true` only when at least one shipper is read and the writer is neither the pair of, nor meets (`permissionSetHoldersMeet`), any shipper. A write naming no package, an unknown or namespace-less writer, a shared platform namespace, a platform-requested name and an unreadable shipper list all stay sealed. Every shipper is judged. Nothing the door accepted on `main` is refused: the diff adds no refusal.
- **Store write intent (`protocol-save.ts`, `promoteDraftForPublish`) — widening, declared right.** `override-artifact` becomes `runtime-only` under the same verdict, so the store's seal and the save door's seal cannot disagree on these two paths. The draft save reads `request.packageId`, so a draft that names no package stays sealed.
- **Lock gate (`packaged-permission-set-lock-gate.ts`) — widening, declared right.** The skip needs a stated writer and a `packaged` verdict in which no declarer is overridden. An `unknown` classification still reaches `assertPermissionSetNotPackageDeclared`. The gate and the seal read the same two predicates; if they ever differ, either one still refuses.
- **`MetadataAuthoringGateContext.packageId` (exported from the package index) — additive optional field, declared right.** `runAuthoringGate` passes it only as a non-empty string. Every registered gate now receives it on a save and on a restore.
- **Restore doors — no accept-set change, right as described.** `refuseRestoredBodyTheSaveDoorRefuses` now hands the gate the row binding, so the lock no longer refuses a package's own set there. Rollback and both revert limbs (`protocol-package-commits.ts`, three sites) still compute the name-wide intent, so the store still refuses. The changeset says so.
- **`isOwnPermissionSetWrite`** is exported from its module only, not from `index.ts`: not public surface. Right.
- **`Metadata-protocol: none` — right.** No key, accepted value or type of a metadata body changes; the change is which address a door admits.

S1 (should-fix) — `undoLandedPromotions` in `protocol-history-and-publish.ts` (a file this diff edits) still computes the write intent from `isArtifactBacked` alone. This is a fourth name-wide site, and neither the PR body nor the changeset lists it. The PR makes its input reachable: a package's own permission-set draft beside another namespace's shipper can now be stored and promoted. Read from the code, not run: when a batch publish is refused on an engine that cannot roll back, the undo of that item passes `override-artifact` to `restoreVersion`, or to the `put` that returns the consumed draft, and `SysMetadataRepository.assertAllowed` refuses both for `permission`. The item then lands in `notUndone` (reported, not silent), and the author's draft is not put back. Required: narrow that line with the same verdict (`item.packageId` is in hand), or name the site in the declared out-of-scope list and its follow-up card. This fails closed, so it is not a security finding.

N1 (nit) — `PermissionSetLockGateContext`, exported from `@objectstack/plugin-security`'s index, also gains the optional `packageId`. The `Clause-②:` line and the changeset name only `MetadataAuthoringGateContext`. Additive and covered by the patch; one clause in the changeset would complete the list.

N2 (nit) — the `Clause-②:` line reads "a save, a draft save or a draft's publish" in the PR body and "a save (or a draft's publish)" in the changeset. Same arm and the same doors (the changeset prose names the draft save); align the two.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/34226-permission-set-seal-by-package.md`: `patch` on `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` and `@objectstack/plugin-security`. These are the two packages whose published source the diff moves. `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` publishes nothing.
- `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is line-initial in both the PR body and the changeset, with the same arm. Correct: a refused save becomes accepted, and an exported context type gains an optional field. There is no narrowing arm, so no BREAKING banner or ADR-0087 marker is owed.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch` under AGENTS.md rule 3 (a non-protocol widening ships `patch`). The level matches.
- `Check Changeset` is green on this head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Check-runs on the head: no red. All 51 are `success` or `skipped` (the skipped ones are UI, docs, opt-in and queue-verdict jobs).
- The dev's NOT MEASURED items (the package suites and the typecheck of `metadata-protocol` and `plugin-security`) are now carried by green `Test Core` (8 shards), `TypeScript Type Check` and `Type Check · workspace` on this head.
- Dev deviations (report 6912081873): the file surface grew past the claim (`protocol.ts` and four more protocol files) with the area seat's approval. The `protocol.ts` change is one optional field on a private event type. The ledger ratchet 1 → 2 matches the new pinned `findOne` double. Accepted.
- `open_questions` is empty. `security_findings: none`: nothing I read contradicts it.
- Acceptance: item 1 holds (both arms, both registration orders, the pair pin; ten ablation legs reported red). Item 2 is answered in the PR body (H3 list). Item 3 is declared.
- Follow-up cards owed and not yet filed (hand-off 6912108122): the three rollback/revert intent sites, and the other sealed package-scoped types. S1's site belongs with the first. Escalated to the dispatching seat: file them before the card closes.
- Overlap: PR #34238 edits the same `promoteDraftForPublish` host `Pick` line; the second to land takes the union.
- SQL push-down: no new id materialisation and no in-app join. The new reads are in-memory registry lookups.
- The PR is a draft, and its author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`.
